intended_object: For a D-equivariant map f : M → N, the map f^{⊗ι} : ⨂_{i∈ι} M → ⨂_{i∈ι} N, viewed as an intertwining map between the wreath-product representations of (ι → D) ⋊ Perm ι on the tensor powers. This is the action on morphisms of the wreath-tensor functor used for tensor induction (Evens). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The underlying linear map is `PiTensorProduct.map (fun _ ↦ f)`, which is f^{⊗ι}. On a pure tensor it sends ⊗ m i to ⊗ f(m i). The intertwining property is proved in the definition. It checks that applying f in every factor commutes with acting by a(i) in each factor and with permuting the factors. This is the standard way the tensor-power/wreath construction acts on morphisms, and the construction is functorial in this way.

The generality matches the underlying `Representation.wreathTensor`: any commutative semiring R, any group D and any index type ι. Mathlib has no wreath-product tensor representation and no corresponding functoriality, so there is no broader counterpart to cite.
